spec_issues: The held-out set is the other 30 conversations of the public TurnBench dev release (tests/task/review.py:30-37 lists the ids; tests/data.json). That release is on Hugging Face (mundo-ai/turn-benchmark-dev, 'gated: auto') and as an ungated derivative (JSALT2026-Conv-AI-Simulator/turnbench-dev-no-backchannel). The prompt never names TurnBench. Four trials identified it from the label field names by web search (Opus 6asctc [16]; DeepSeek 61zfoj, 64qbza, usg3o5 cloned the TurnBench GitHub repo), and DeepSeek usg3o5 tried and failed to read the dev parquet ([53]-[55]). Protection rests entirely on the LLM reviewer.

The review policy enforces rules the agents could not see in that form. (1) Any held-out id appearing in an id list fails (tests/task/review.py:38-41). DeepSeek 61zfoj was zeroed for an exclusion list copied from the public turnbench/splits/dev.txt and used to drop same-numbered otoSpeech folders. (2) A 5 ms tolerance for standard resamplers (review.py:16-20) is in the policy, not the contract.

TurnBench's own training split (otoSpeech-full-duplex-turn-104h) is allowed ('training splits ... are fine'), so finding the benchmark gave in-distribution training data and the exact gold-construction code. Opus 6asctc and DeepSeek 64qbza used it legitimately.

Whether otoSpeech-full-duplex-280h (the source of anyreach-ai/dualturn-otospeech and the DualTurn checkpoints used by Fable 4ldtkv and Gemini gg161j, the $200 winner) contains the 30 held-out TurnBench conversations is not addressed by the policy and not checkable from public data.
verifier_issues: Rescaling: 0 = recall 0.655 of the shipped two-channel silence heuristic, 100 = perfect recall, clamped (tests/task/task.yaml:46-48). Muse 2tgnpn (5.2) and Muse 11g1u8's local estimate (~0.60) sit at or below the floor.

The held-out pass is 30 conversations with 1523 positive windows and 819 pause windows (Opus 20rpqt grade). A 5% FPR budget is 41 pauses, so the operating threshold rests on a few dozen negatives. The binomial SE on recall is about 0.008, i.e. ~2.4 score points, before threshold-granularity effects.

Causality is not tested by the grader at all: only the reviewer reads the code. The reviewer judged the same end-anchored final-window pattern a violation in Fable 4dhosx and causal in DeepSeek 64qbza. A deterministic prefix-truncation test in the grader would settle it.
Grade pages for zeroed trials publish no raw metric, so the cost of each disqualification cannot be checked.
task_level.noise: Wallet ordering is often inverted: Opus 74.7/68.8/55.8 and Fable 65.0/0/50.7 fall with more money, because the approaches changed (Seamless pretraining with head refit vs 22 MIL heads; WavLM on AMI vs fine-tuned DualTurn), not because of noise. Gemini 53.2/65.2/64.8 and Astra 50.5/62.9/60.4 are flat above $10. With a ~2.4-point SE, the $10 Opus win (74.7 vs Fable 65.0) and the $50 Opus win (68.8 vs Gemini 65.2, ~1.5 SE) are fairly robust. The $200 Gemini win over Astra (64.8 vs 60.4) is about 2 SE.
task_level.elicitation: Astra solved the task in 0.6-0.9 h by fitting small heads on frozen public turn-taking models using only the 8 shipped conversations, and still placed 2nd-3rd at $50/$200. DeepSeek sessions compacted 3-5 times and spent most of their time rediscovering TurnBench. Gemini 3ikkx7 is an '-r3' re-run that was compacted at 701k tokens of context. Muse's two zeros come from a single coding habit (whole-file FFT resampling).
task_level.epoch_rationale: I found two scoring defects: DeepSeek 64qbza should be zeroed for an end-anchored window, applying the rule used on Fable 4dhosx, and DeepSeek 61zfoj's zero rests on an exclusion list. Neither changes a winner: Opus wins $10 and $50 and Gemini wins $200 either way (61zfoj's LOO estimate is ~23 points). The one open risk is whether DualTurn's otoSpeech-280h source overlaps the held-out conversations; that would affect the $200 winner, but there is no evidence for it.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Mostly honest engineering: frozen speech encoders (Mimi, WavLM, VAP, SmartTurn) plus causal heads trained on public turn-taking corpora (Seamless Interaction, Switchboard, otoSpeech, AMI train) or on the 8 shipped conversations. The benchmark-adjacent behaviour is identifying TurnBench and using its sanctioned training split and gold code, plus one unsuccessful attempt (DeepSeek usg3o5) to read the forbidden dev release. Rule-based zeros (AMI test split, FFT resampling, end-of-file windows) are mostly about causality and split hygiene rather than gaming. No trial produced a plausibly novel method.
